The first proposed logarithm conformal mapping is w(z) = z + 4Log[z-1] - 4Log[z+1].
The second proposed logarithm conformal mapping is w(z) = z + 4Log[z+1] - 4Log[z-1].
The refractive index range for the conformal cloaks based on the first mapping is 0 to 9.839.
The refractive index range for the conformal cloaks based on the second mapping is 0 to 22.043.
The authors apply two kissing mirrored Maxwell's fish-eye lenses in the lower Riemann sheet of the virtual space to further reduce the maximum refractive index value.
The radii of the mirrored Maxwell's fish-eye lenses are set as r1 = λ/2π = 5.53697 for the first mapping and r2 = λ/2π = 5.77259 for the second mapping.
The authors observe good cloaking effects at the eigen-frequencies of the kissing mirrored Maxwell's fish-eye lenses, given by f = 2πrc/√(l^2 - 1), where l is an integer.
The branch cut in the virtual space connects the upper and lower Riemann sheets and determines the refractive index distribution and cloaking behavior in the physical space.
The symmetric properties of the conformal mappings and the mirrored Maxwell's fish-eye lenses help lower the refractive index distribution and optimize the cloaking performance.
The authors suggest the proposed conformal mappings could potentially be used for other applications, such as an artificial electromagnetic wormhole.
Numerical simulations using the finite element method are performed to confirm the theoretical analysis.
The authors mention that the maximum refractive index value could potentially be reduced even further by proposing new conformal mappings.
